record.tranche_reason: The post gives a specific argument that SAE features may be combinations rather than the target model's atomic features, and that feature splitting may reflect SAE incentives rather than the target model's representation. It reports no systematic test of the claim; limited experimental results appear in comments.
record.gate_note: The main post's toy examples and discussion of Anthropic's feature-splitting results are hypothetical or cited findings, not results from this post, so they are not rows. Rows below record experiments and measurements reported in comments. The post proposes orthogonality regularization but does not test it itself.
record.test_reason: The main post gives a specific argument against V5: L1-trained SAEs may learn common feature combinations instead of atomic features and may miss rare ones. It reads feature splitting as an SAE artefact. One comment (Glen Taggart) reports a toy SAE with known orthogonal ground-truth features that learned no atomic feature. That bears directly on V5. Everything else is argument, cited results or method-performance numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author argues that L1 sparsity incentives can make SAEs learn common feature combinations rather than atomic 'true features' and drop rare features. He argues feature splitting likely reflects this artefact, not the model's true feature structure. He proposes, but does not test, a decoder orthogonality regularizer, along with tests comparing SAEs trained with and without it.
record.recipe_differences: The post offers a conceptual analysis of SAE training and proposes an orthogonality regularizer; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The argument says the outcome may depend on feature frequencies, feature co-occurrence and activation proportions, SAE width, and the L1 regularization weight. The commenter-reported regularizer experiment changes reconstruction score and L0.

fits_no_version.finding: An orthogonality regularizer on a 1-layer-model SAE changed reconstruction score from 0.846 to 0.828, with L0 going from ~17 to ~18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonality regularization of SAE decoders costs little reconstruction at similar sparsity in one small run.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT2-Small layer-10 SAE decoder features are much less orthogonal than random directions, at max, 10th and 100th nearest neighbours.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary directions in LLMs are geometrically clustered beyond chance.

record.problems: The main post's central account is an argument illustrated by hypothetical examples, not a controlled experiment. The reported comment experiments are preliminary or minimally described; several values are only in plots not present in the text. The post relies on findings from other work for its discussion of feature splitting.
record.rows_left_out: Cited findings from Anthropic's SAE paper were not included as rows because they are results from other work. The post's hypothetical diagrams and illustrative code snippets were not treated as experimental outcomes.

untested.parts: Stability across seeds or runs, and completeness in real LLM SAEs. The LLM-side claims (feature splitting as combinations, missed rare features) are argued from Anthropic's cited results, not tested.
Not tested: no toy superposition geometry or sparsity transition.
Not tested: no measurement of LLM features spread across neurons.

missing.what: A second, larger toy example of the same composite-feature phenomenon (figure only, same setup).
missing.locator: Comment by Glen Taggart, 'Edit: Remembered I have a larger example'

missing.what: Cosine-similarity histogram of the regularized SAE, with peaks near 0.3 and 0.05. Figure only; the commenter calls the superposition reading speculative.

record.verdict_notes: The post itself has no experiments; its toy diagrams are hypothetical. The only V5-relevant evidence is a commenter's minimal toy run (r6), so the challenge is weak and confined to that toy setting. Reliance on Anthropic's feature-splitting results is citation, not test.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled test of toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.

The post argues that SAE sparsity incentives and limited capacity can favor feature combinations, but does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity independent of capacity pressure.
No test that LLM features are spread across neurons or that SAEs recover the model's actual sparse features.
The post argues that SAE features may be composites and may miss rare features, but does not empirically test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
No test of whether the model's superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
